## What this letter says

This letter gives the results of a scan of your left knee. The scan was an MRI. An MRI is a scan that uses magnets to take detailed pictures inside the body. The letter also gives the plan from your bone and joint surgeon (orthopaedic surgeon).

The scan found:

- There may be a small tear in the inner cartilage of your left knee. It is at the back part (posterior horn of the medial meniscus). A tear is only possible. The letter says a tear cannot be ruled out.
- There is no broken bone (no fracture).
- The ACL is a ligament inside your knee. Its full name is anterior cruciate ligament. The letter says it is whole (intact).
- There is mild early wear and tear on the inner side of the knee (osteoarthritis).
- There is a little fluid in the knee (small joint effusion).

Surgery is not planned at this stage.

## What you need to do

1. Mr Osei has sent you for physiotherapy. It lasts 6 to 8 weeks.
2. Mr Osei will see you again in the bone and joint clinic (orthopaedic clinic). This will be in 3 months.
3. You can carry on with normal activities as far as the pain allows.

## Dates and medicines

- 1 September 2026: you had the MRI scan of your left knee.
- 6 to 8 weeks: how long the physiotherapy lasts.
- In 3 months: Mr Osei will see you in the orthopaedic clinic.

The letter does not list any medicines.

## Questions to ask your doctor

1. What does "medial meniscus" mean?
2. What will happen at physiotherapy?
3. What does the early wear and tear (osteoarthritis) mean for my knee?
4. Can you tell me more about the possible tear?

## When to get urgent help

The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
